title: The computer understands variable names
statement: The name of a variable tells the computer what it is for, so a variable called total will add things up and one called largest will hold the biggest value.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: predict the value of a descriptively named variable that is never updated
evidence_patterns.signature: predicts the value the name suggests rather than the value assigned

example.item:
largest = 0
for n in [4, 9, 2]:
    pass
print(largest)

discriminators.vs_slip: The prediction follows the name on every item, and renaming the variable to x changes the learner's answer. A slip does not depend on the name.

conflicts_with.label: Identifiers are labels with no meaning to the machine

resolved_by.label: Identifiers are labels with no meaning to the machine
The machine does exactly what the code says

sources.citation: Pea, R. D. (1986). Language-independent conceptual "bugs" in novice programming. Journal of Educational Computing Research, 2(1), 25-36.
sources.note: Egocentrism bug: attributing interpretive intelligence to the machine.

sources.citation: Sorva, J. (2012). Visual Program Simulation in Introductory Programming Education (Doctoral dissertation, Aalto University). Appendix A catalogues introductory programming misconceptions from the literature.
